products.name: Grammarly for Education
products.note: Institutional writing support; student data; FERPA compliance; generative AI features

profile_text.body:
Grammarly is a for-profit company founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its website describes it as an AI writing assistance platform that provides personalized guidance, text generation, grammar correction, and tone suggestions across apps and websites. The company states that it does not sell or monetize user content, provide it for advertising purposes, or allow third-party service providers to train their models on user content.

The company offers two tracked products: Grammarly, a general writing and editing tool that reads document text broadly, and Grammarly for Education, an institutional version designed for student use that includes generative AI features and is described as FERPA-compliant. The site claims that organizations deploying Grammarly save an average of $5,000 per employee per year, and references a product called Superhuman Go as a delivery vehicle that combines writing support with productivity agents.

The held facts indicate Grammarly has 174 points of legal exposure mapped to California, though no specific cases are on record in this site's data.
